newsitem.title: GERMANY: Paris wants Camdessus to be first ECB head - paper.
newsitem.headline: Paris wants Camdessus to be first ECB head - paper.

text.p: France still wants a Frenchman to become the first president of the European Central Bank (ECB) and has proposed to Germany that Michel Camdessus, head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), should take the post, a German newspaper reported on Tuesday.
In return, France has offered to support a German candidate to replace Camdessus at the IMF, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reported, citing unnamed sources in Germany and France.
The report said France continued to oppose the appointment of Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg as first ECB president.
Duisenberg will succeed Alexandre Lamfalussy as president of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the ECB, in mid-1997.

France is the only European Union member to have said that Duisenberg's appointment does not mean he will go on to head the ECB, the paper said. But it added that Duisenberg could count on the support of most EU nations.
The paper said France wanted a Frenchman to head the ECB as compensation for the bank being located in Frankfurt, Germany's financial capital.
In addition, Duisenberg is regarded by some French decision-makers as being too close to the Bundesbank in his monetary policy thinking, the paper said.
Germany regards France's proposal as a last attempt to change Bonn's mind since it is evident that Germany supports Duisenberg, it added.
But the paper said that informed sources saw two objections against a candidacy by Camdessus.
Firstly, France's attempt to sweeten Camdessus' appointment by backing a German candidate for the IMF post was all too transparent and it was not up to France to allocate the IMF position anyway.
Secondly, such a move would raise the suspicion among the other EU partners that Germany and France wanted to dominate EU policy, the paper said.
